description: Nestled in the heart of vibrant Back Bay, our studio offers a comfortable haven for travelers eager to explore all that Boston has to offer. neighborhood_overview:
Back Bay is one of Boston’s most iconic and walkable neighborhoods, known for its historic brownstones, upscale shopping, and vibrant dining scene. Stroll along Newbury Street (2-minute walk), where designer boutiques, art galleries, and charming cafés are nestled in elegant brick townhouses. Just a short walk away, Copley Square (7-minute walk) is home to the historic Trinity Church and the stunning Boston Public Library, whose European-style courtyard is a must-see. Tree-lined Commonwealth Avenue, inspired by the grand boulevards of Paris, showcases some of the city’s most beautiful mansions.

For sports fans, Fenway Park is just a 10-minute walk (0.5 miles) away. Catch a Red Sox game, attend a concert, or take a tour of one of America’s oldest ballparks. The Hynes Convention Center is also nearby, just a 0.4-mile walk, making this a convenient stay for business travelers.

Back Bay offers plenty of ways to spend an afternoon. Take a stroll along the Charles River

Along Newbury Street, well-heeled locals frequent designer boutiques, fashion chains, art galleries and patio cafes set in elegant brick townhouses. Expansive Copley Square is flanked by 1800s landmarks Trinity Church and the Boston Public Library. Mansions dot the neighborhood’s tree-lined streets, many on Paris-inspired Commonwealth Avenue."


Things to do!

Fenway Park - Just a 1-mile walk! Check out a Sox game, or concert, or go for a tour of one of America's oldest ballparks.

Hynes Convention Center - .8 mile walk, the perfect spot if you are in town for a convention!

Boylston Street is Newbury’s busy commercial neighborhood, and generally speaking, Newbury is more pedestrian-friendly. When Covid struck our world, we were at a standstill! We had to quickly learn and grow to make sure our health and cleaning standards were in line with those of the CDC. We remain dedicated to providing a happy and healthy stay for our amazing guests!

We are partnered with a wonderful non-profit that specializes in providing  housing for families in need of a discounted or free place to stay for the duration of their hospital visits. If you are here for a hospital related visit, please let us know prior to booking! 

We hope we get the chance to host you!

neighborhood_overview:
Harvard Square (8-minute drive):

Harvard Square isn’t just a place – it’s a storybook of American history and culture with pages that unfold at every corner. This area has been a meeting point for intellectuals, artists, and revolutionaries for centuries. It was the site of the first printing press in British North America in 1638, producing works like the “Bay Psalm Book”. During the abolitionist movement, the square was a hub for activism and later a focal point for anti-war protests in the 20th century.

Key attractions include the Harvard Art Museums, where you can view masterpieces by Vincent van Gogh (Self-Portrait Dedicated to Paul Gauguin), Claude Monet (La Japonaise), and Georgia O’Keeffe (Red Hills, Grey Sky). Nearby, the Harvard Museum of Natural History showcases the renowned Glass Flowers collection, intricately crafted models of over 4,000 plant species​

For bookworms, the Harvard Book Store is a literary paradise with shelves of rare find

Cultural & Historic Sites
• Samuel Adams Brewery – A must-visit for beer lovers, offering brewery tours and tastings of craft beer.

• Footlight Club – America’s oldest community theater, staging local performances.
